C-WORKFLOW-PROMPT-SYNC-DOCTOR-ARCHIVE.Summary: Close the verified agent-facing workflow protocol, managed-prompt sync, doctor drift, skill-root deduplication, and archive-aggregate gaps, then prepare the 2.4.0 release.
C-WORKFLOW-PROMPT-SYNC-DOCTOR-ARCHIVE.Problem: Three independent surfaces are incomplete. Managed skill and agent instructions do not consistently describe the exact tracked launch header or the controller-only ownership of work items, so workers are told to use a tool they cannot call and controllers are not shown the literal first-line contract. The managed prompt sync cannot reconcile legacy inline {file:...} managed system prompts after the V2 native-markdown migration, and doctor does not report prompt drift, duplicate skill roots, or the inert apply_patch permission action. The vv-reflect extractor is single-session only, so machine-wide questions require rewriting an ad-hoc aggregator that is easy to double-count across the legacy part table and session_message.

Goals.Goal: Make the tracked launch protocol executable from the shipped instructions: literal VVOC_WORK_ITEM_ID first line, state-to-agent map, standalone field rules, review_only handling, and explicit recovery from launch rejections.
Teach workers to copy the assignment header verbatim and never open, list, or close work items themselves.
Reconcile legacy inline managed {file:...} system prompts during sync, preserving user-owned files and reporting the source when management is not possible.
Add read-only doctor checks for managed prompt drift, duplicate skill roots, and deprecated permission actions without failing open on missing {file:...} references.
Canonicalize and deduplicate the skills[] roots by real path while preserving user order and unrelated entries.
Add a streaming archive mode to the vv-reflect extractor with call-id deduplication, filters, deterministic aggregates, and JSON/Markdown output.
Correct the documented managed-agent path to the native OpenCode discovery location and prepare a 2.4.0 package/schema/changelog release.

Constraints.Constraint: Preserve all existing workflow state transitions, authorization gates, review obligations, recovery budgets, persisted state version, and native tool names.
Do not weaken fail-closed V1 migration: report-only and unmappable OpenCode fields continue to abort sync with a manual checklist. Only improve the diagnostic wording where needed.
Managed prompt writes remain conservative: user-owned files are never overwritten, managed files keep their managed marker, and inline system overrides continue to win over generated markdown.
Doctor additions are read-only and produce warnings for drift, duplicate roots, and deprecated permission actions; missing {file:...} references remain problems with a non-zero exit.
Skill deduplication must preserve the first occurrence, preserve unrelated strings, and never silently delete a real directory or non-symlink skill copy.
The archive extractor remains standard-library-only, opens the database read-only, never reads message text for aggregates, and never doubles legacy part and session_message rows.
No generated dist edits. Native dependency pins, canonical vvoc schema v3, persisted workflow snapshot version 4, and public exports remain unchanged.
The release is prepared locally to 2.4.0 with package/schema/changelog consistency and full gates; npm publication through the CI workflow is not performed from this environment.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No new workflow tool, state, mode, authority stage, or persisted-state format.
No automatic deletion of user-owned inline agents, skill directories, or permission rules.
No generic allowlist that claims to validate every future native permission action; only curated deprecated aliases are reported.
No replacement of the session-scoped extractor output or its existing target-resolution behavior.
No npm publish, CI dispatch, git tag push, or GitHub Release creation from this environment.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: AC-01: The shipped vv-execute and vv-review instructions contain the literal `VVOC_WORK_ITEM_ID: wi-<n>` contract, a state-to-allowed-agent map, the standalone permitted-field rule, the review_only new-item rule, and the single-agent-per-state rejection guidance.

AC-02: vv-implementer, vv-code-reviewer, and vv-spec-reviewer tell the worker to copy the header from the assignment and state that the controller owns work-item lifecycle; no worker template claims work_item_open is available to the worker.

AC-03: work_item_open's model-facing description lists the standalone fields and the generic-task-only fields, and the shipped contract tests assert that wording without claiming that validation returns only one issue.
AC-04: sync updates a vvoc-managed legacy inline {file:...} system prompt to the current template body, preserves user-owned files, and reports the source when an inline system file is not managed.

AC-05: doctor reports stale managed agent prompts and managed skills, duplicate skills[] roots after real-path normalization, and the inert apply_patch permission action as warnings; a missing {file:...} reference remains a problem.
AC-06: skills[] deduplication keeps one canonical root per real path, preserves first-occurrence order and unrelated entries, and leaves a user-owned skill directory untouched.

AC-07: session-graph.py supports an archive mode with since/until/project/agent/skill filters, top limits, JSON and Markdown output, streaming aggregation, and call-id deduplication; the archive totals do not sum legacy part and session_message rows.

AC-08: README and GRACE context identify the native managed-agent prompt location correctly, the release is 2.4.0 across package.json, schema $id, and CHANGELOG, and typecheck, lint, format, GRACE markup, contract checks, tests, build, pack check, release check, grace lint, and grace status pass on the final snapshot.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: bun test src/lib/managed-agents.test.ts src/lib/managed-skills.test.ts src/lib/opencode.test.ts src/lib/session-graph.test.ts src/commands/doctor.test.ts src/commands/sync.test.ts src/plugins/workflow/contracts.test.ts
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Targeted suites prove the instruction, migration, doctor, deduplication, and extractor behavior; the full gate and release:check prove the 2.4.0 package surface; GRACE lint/status prove the durable projections.

Assumptions.Assumption: The user explicitly requested all three fix blocks autonomously and a 2.4.0 release in the current conversation; this authorizes the approved lifecycle and direct implementation without a separate review checkpoint.
The legacy inline {file:...} prompt is vvoc-managed when the target file carries the managed marker and the inline value is a single file token; otherwise sync treats it as user-owned.
The local environment cannot publish to npm or dispatch the release workflow, so 2.4.0 is prepared and verified locally, not published.
